chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He used to say: 'Whoever flees from two men in battle during the infantry advance has truly fled, and whoever flees from three men in battle during the infantry advance has not fled.'

key_terms.الزَّحْفِ: Infantry advance or walking battle formation

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on fleeing from two or three soldiers during battle?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the jurisprudential threshold for lawful retreat (firar) during infantry combat, distinguishing between fleeing from two soldiers, which invalidates the retreat, and fleeing from three, which is permissible. This ruling reflects the practical military logic of the time, where a small group could effectively hold off a larger force, thereby setting a clear legal boundary for when cowardice versus strategic withdrawal applies.
